title: Case #3: The Midnight Prescriptions
summary: Morphine is leaving St. Wren's under a doctor's name. Join the tables until the real hand appears.

steps.title: Case #3
body: St. Wren's pharmacy is **short on morphine**. The paperwork is clean: every dose was prescribed through the system, and most carry the name of **Dr. Felix Haag**, a neurologist with a spotless record. He says he has no idea what anyone is talking about.
Rosa: *"Systems record who typed a login, not whose hands were on the keyboard. Join the prescription log to everything else and see which rows don't fit."*

steps.title: Clue 1: the morphine trail
prompt: List every **Morphine** prescription with the prescriber's name: **id**, **prescriber**, **day**, **hour**, in day then hour order.

Tables: `staff(id, name, role)`, `shifts(staff_id, day, start_hour, end_hour, location)` (on shift when `start_hour <= hour < end_hour`), `terminals(id, location)`, `ward_patients(id, name, discharged)`, `rx_log(id, staff_id, patient_id, drug, day, hour, terminal)`.
solution: SELECT r.id, s.name AS prescriber, r.day, r.hour
JOIN staff AS s ON s.id = r.staff_id

steps.explain: Seven morphine prescriptions. Three of Dr. Haag's were written at 1, 2 and 3 in the morning.

steps.title: Clue 2: off the clock
prompt: Find the morphine prescriptions written when the prescriber was **not on shift**: no `shifts` row for that staff member on that day covering that hour.
Return **id**, **day**, **hour** and **terminal**. Use a LEFT JOIN anti-join (or NOT EXISTS).

Tables: `staff(id, name, role)`, `shifts(staff_id, day, start_hour, end_hour, location)` (on shift when `start_hour <= hour < end_hour`), `terminals(id, location)`, `ward_patients(id, name, discharged)`, `rx_log(id, staff_id, patient_id, drug, day, hour, terminal)`.
solution: ON sh.staff_id = r.staff_id AND sh.day = r.day
AND r.hour >= sh.start_hour AND r.hour < sh.end_hour
WHERE r.drug = 'Morphine' AND sh.staff_id IS NULL;

steps.title: Clue 3: where did it go?
prompt: For those three prescriptions (ids **3, 6 and 8**), return the **id**, the terminal's **location**, the **patient** name and the patient's **discharged** date.

Tables: `staff(id, name, role)`, `shifts(staff_id, day, start_hour, end_hour, location)` (on shift when `start_hour <= hour < end_hour`), `terminals(id, location)`, `ward_patients(id, name, discharged)`, `rx_log(id, staff_id, patient_id, drug, day, hour, terminal)`.
solution: SELECT r.id, t.location, p.name AS patient, p.discharged
JOIN terminals AS t ON t.id = r.terminal
JOIN ward_patients AS p ON p.id = r.patient_id

steps.title: Name the culprit
prompt: Who was **on shift in the Pharmacy** at the time of **all three** suspicious prescriptions (ids 3, 6 and 8)?
Join those prescriptions to the shifts that cover their day and hour **in the Pharmacy**, and return the **name** of the staff member who matches all three.

Tables: `staff(id, name, role)`, `shifts(staff_id, day, start_hour, end_hour, location)` (on shift when `start_hour <= hour < end_hour`), `terminals(id, location)`, `ward_patients(id, name, discharged)`, `rx_log(id, staff_id, patient_id, drug, day, hour, terminal)`.
solution: ON sh.day = r.day AND r.hour >= sh.start_hour AND r.hour < sh.end_hour
JOIN staff AS s ON s.id = sh.staff_id

Group by staff and keep the one with `COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) = 3`.
steps.explain: **Perrin Vos**, pharmacy technician, was alone on the night shift for all three, using a login he'd watched Dr. Haag type. Joss Kader and Tilly Brook were each there for only one. Dr. Haag's name is cleared.
